title: Surviving Partial Failure and Change — Check

questions.prompt: Why prefer `Promise.allSettled` over `Promise.all` in a gateway that composes several services?
questions.explanation: `allSettled` waits for all calls and reports each result independently, enabling graceful degradation when one upstream fails.
options: It runs the calls sequentially for safety
It returns every call's outcome so one failure doesn't sink the whole response
It is the only method that supports timeouts

questions.prompt: If six independent services each have 99% availability and the gateway requires all six to succeed, the combined success rate is lower than 99%.
questions.explanation: Requiring all six multiplies the probabilities: 0.99^6 is about 94%, lower than any single service.

questions.prompt: What problem does wrapping each upstream call in a timeout solve?
questions.explanation: With concurrency, total latency is the slowest call; a timeout converts a stalled call into a handled failure instead of an indefinite wait.
options: It reduces the number of upstream services
It prevents a single hung service from pinning the entire response open
It removes the need for the gateway

questions.prompt: How does an anti-corruption layer in each `lib/` module help with versioning?
questions.explanation: By translating each upstream into an internal vocabulary, schema churn is absorbed in one module instead of rippling through the system.
options: It exposes the raw upstream schema directly to the UI
It translates upstream schema changes into the gateway's stable vocabulary so downstream code is unaffected
It deletes old API versions automatically
It forces the UI to update on every upstream change
